80:1: Interpretation of Surah Abasa In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful More than one of the commentators mentioned that one day the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was addressing some of the leaders of the Quraysh and he hoped that he would convert to Islam. While he was addressing him and whispering to him, Ibn Umm Maktum, who had been among those who had converted to Islam long ago, came and began asking the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about something and insisting on him. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, wished that he could spare that moment so that he could address that man, hoping and desiring that he would be guided. And he frowned at Ibn Umm Maktum, turned away from him and turned to the other man, so God revealed: He frowned and turned away * When the blind man came to him * And what do you know that perhaps he may be purified? That is, he will attain purity and self-purification. Or be reminded and the reminder will benefit him. That is, he will attain admonition and be deterred from forbidden things. But as for him who is self-sufficient, * To him you attend. That is, as for the rich, you approach him that perhaps he may be guided. And it is not upon you that he does not purify. That is, you are not required to do so if he does not attain purity. But as for him who comes to you striving * And he fears, that is, he intends you and follows you in order to be guided by what you say to him, You are distracted from him. That is, you are preoccupied. From here, God the Almighty commanded His Messenger (peace and blessings of God be upon him) not to single out anyone for warning, but rather to treat the noble and the weak, the poor and the rich, the masters and the slaves, the men and women, the young and the old, then God the Almighty guides whomever He wills to the straight path, and He has the perfect wisdom and the conclusive proof. Al-Hafiz Ayu Ya`la said in his Musnad: Muhammad bin Mahdi told us, Abd al-Razzaq told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Anas, may God be pleased with him, regarding the words of God Almighty: He frowned and turned away, Ibn Umm Maktum came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was speaking to Ubayy bin Khalaf, so he turned away from him. Then God Almighty revealed: He frowned and turned away, because the blind man came to him, and after that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, would honor him. Qatada said: Anas bin Malik told me: I saw him on the day of Al-Qadisiyyah wearing a suit of armor and carrying a black banner, meaning Ibn Umm Maktum. Abu Ya’la and Ibn Jarir said: Sa’id bin Yahya Al-Umawi told us, my father told me: This is what we presented to Hisham bin Urwah on the authority of his father on the authority of Aisha who said: He frowned and turned away was revealed about the blind Ibn Umm Maktum. “He came to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and kept saying, ‘Guide me.’ She said: And with the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was a man from the leaders of the polytheists. She said: The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) kept turning away from him and turning to the other one and saying, ‘Do you see anything wrong with what I am saying?’ He said, ‘No!’ It was for this that ‘He frowned and turned away’ was revealed.” Al-Tirmidhi narrated this hadith on the authority of Sa’id bin Yahya Al-Umawi with a similar chain of transmission. Then he said: Some of them narrated it on the authority of Hisham bin Urwah on the authority of his father who said: He frowned and turned away was revealed about Ibn Umm Maktum and did not mention Aisha in it. I said This is how it is in Al-Muwatta’. Then Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated through Al-Awfi from Ibn Abbas, his saying: He frowned and turned away * Because the blind man came to him. He said: “While the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was conversing with Utbah ibn Rabi’ah, Abu Jahl ibn Hisham, and Al-Abbas ibn Abdul Muttalib, and he was often confronting them and was eager for them to believe, a blind man called Abdullah ibn Umm Maktum came walking towards him while he was conversing with them. Abdullah began to recite a verse from the Qur’an to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, teach me from what God has taught you. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, turned away from him, frowned in his face, turned away, and disliked his words, and turned to the others. When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had finished his conversation and was about to return to his family, God took away some of his sight and he shook his head. Then God, the Most High, revealed: “He frowned and turned away * Because the blind man came to him. And what do you know that he may be purified * Or that he may be reminded and the reminder may benefit him?”” When what was revealed about him was revealed, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, honored him and spoke to him and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: What is your need? Do you want anything? - and when he left him, he would say: Do you have a need for anything? This is because God, the Most High, revealed: “But he who is self-sufficient, you attend to him. And it is not to do with you that he should not be purified.”” There is strangeness and oddity in it, and its chain of transmission has been criticized. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad bin Mansur al-Ramadi told us, Abdullah bin Salih told us, al-Layth told us, Yunus told me, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, who said: Salim bin Abdullah said, on the authority of Abdullah bin Umar, who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: Bilal calls the adhan at night, so eat and drink until you hear the adhan of Ibn Umm Maktum, who is the blind man about whom God, the Most High, revealed: He frowned and turned away, because the blind man came to him. And he used to call the adhan with Bilal. Salim said: He was a blind man, so he would not call the adhan until the people, when they saw the break of dawn, would say to him, The adhan has begun. Thus, Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, Mujahid, Abu Malik, Qatadah, al-Dahhak, Ibn Zayd, and more than one of the early and later generations mentioned that it was revealed about Ibn Umm Maktum, and it is well-known that his name is Abdullah, and it is also said that it is Amr, and God knows best. And the Almighty’s saying: No indeed! It is a reminder, meaning this surah or the commandment to treat people equally in conveying knowledge, between the noble and the lowly. Qatada and al-Suddi said: No indeed! It is a reminder, meaning the Qur’an. So whoever wills, let him remember it, meaning whoever wills, let him remember God Almighty in all his affairs. It is possible that the pronoun refers back to the revelation, as the statement indicates it. And the Almighty’s saying: In honored scrolls, exalted and purified. That is, this Surah or the sermon, and both are intertwined. Rather, the entire Qur’an is in honored scrolls, that is, revered and respected. Exalted means of high status. Purified that is, from defilement, excess, and deficiency. And the Almighty’s saying: In the hands of scribes. Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Ad-Dahhak, and Ibn Zayd said: They are the angels. Wahb ibn Munabbih said: They are the companions of Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him. Qatadah said: They are the reciters. Ibn Jurayj said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Safrah in Nabataean means the reciters. Ibn Jarir said: The correct view is that the safrah are the angels, and the safrah means between God Almighty and His creation, and from this it is said the ambassador is the one who strives between people for peace and good, as the poet said: I do not leave the embassy among people one day, I walk with deceit if I walk Al-Bukhari said: Safra: The angels, they travel and reconcile between them. When the angels descend with the revelation of God Almighty and deliver it, they are like ambassadors who reconcile between people. God Almighty said: Noble and righteous meaning their creation is noble, good and honorable, and their morals and actions are righteous, pure and complete. From here, the bearer of the Quran should be on the right path and in his actions. Imam Ahmad said: Ismail told us, Hisham told us, on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of Zurarah ibn Awfa, on the authority of Sa’d ibn Hisham, on the authority of Aisha may God be pleased with her, who said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: He who recites the Quran and is proficient in it will be with the noble and righteous scribes, and he who recites it but finds it difficult will have two rewards. Narrated by the group on the authority of Qatadah.

80:15: More than one of the commentators mentioned that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was one day addressing some of the leaders of the Quraysh and he had hoped that he would convert to Islam. And he frowned at Ibn Umm Maktum, turned away from him and turned to the other man, so God revealed: He frowned and turned away * When the blind man came to him * And what do you know that perhaps he may be purified? That is, he will attain purity and self-purification. Or be reminded and the reminder will benefit him. That is, he will attain admonition and be deterred from forbidden things. But as for him who is self-sufficient, * To him you attend. That is, as for the rich, you approach him that perhaps he may be guided. And it is not upon you that he does not purify. That is, you are not required to do so if he does not attain purity. But as for him who comes to you striving * And he fears, that is, he intends you and follows you in order to be guided by what you say to him, You are distracted from him. That is, you are preoccupied. From here, God the Almighty commanded His Messenger (peace and blessings of God be upon him) not to single out anyone for warning, but rather to treat the noble and the weak, the poor and the rich, the masters and the slaves, the men and women, the young and the old, then God the Almighty guides whomever He wills to the straight path, and He has the perfect wisdom and the conclusive proof. 80:17: God Almighty says, blaming those of the children of Adam who deny the resurrection and the Hereafter: How ungrateful is man! Ad-Dahhak said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: How ungrateful is man! Abu Malik said the same: This applies to the human race who denies because of their frequent denial without any basis, but rather due to mere exaggeration and lack of knowledge. Ibn Jurayj said: How ungrateful is he! meaning how intensely ungrateful he is. Ibn Jarir said: It is possible that what is meant is what made him a denier, i.e. what made him deny the Resurrection. Al-Baghawi narrated it on the authority of Muqatil and Al-Kalbi. Qatada said, How ungrateful he is! How cursed he is! Then God explained to him how He created him from something insignificant and that He is able to restore him as He began him. God said, “From what thing did He create him? From a sperm-drop He created him. Then He proportioned for him.” That is, He proportioned his lifespan, his provision, his deeds, and whether he would be wretched or blessed. Then He made the way easy for him. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Then He made his emergence from his mother’s womb easy for him. This is what Ikrimah, Al-Dahhak, Abu Salih, Qatada, and Al-Suddi said, and Ibn Jarir chose it. Mujahid said, This is like the statement of God, the Most High, ‘Indeed, We guided him to the way, be he grateful or ungrateful.’ This is what Al-Hasan and Ibn Zayd said, and this is what is most likely, and God knows best. And the Almighty’s saying: Then He caused him to die and buried him, meaning that after He created him, He caused him to die and buried him, meaning He made him have a grave. The Arabs say: I buried the man if that turned away from him, and God buried him. And I bit the bull’s horn and God bit it. And I cut off the camel’s tail and God cut it off. And I expelled so-and-so from me and God expelled him, meaning He made him an outcast. Al-A’sha said: If she rested a dead person on her chest, he would live and not be transferred to the grave God the Almighty said: Then, if He wills, He will resurrect him meaning He will raise him up after his death. From this we say resurrection and rising again. And among His signs is that He created you from dust; then, suddenly, you are human beings, dispersed 2:11. And look at the bones - how We raise them up and then cover them with flesh 2:11. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Asbagh ibn al-Faraj told us, Ibn Wahb told us, Amr ibn al-Harith told me that Diraj Abu al-Samh told him, on the authority of Abu al-Haytham, on the authority of Abu Sa’id, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: The dust consumes everything of the human being except his coccyx. It was said: What is it, O Messenger of God? He said: Like a mustard seed from which you grow. This hadith is proven in the two Sahihs on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, without this addition. Its wording is: “Every son of Adam will decay except the coccyx. From it he was created and in it he will be rebuilt.” And the Almighty’s saying: No, he has not yet fulfilled what he was commanded. Ibn Jarir said: God Almighty says: No, he has not yet fulfilled what he was commanded. He says: He has not fulfilled the obligations imposed upon him by his Lord, the Almighty and Majestic. Then he and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh on the authority of Mujahid, the Almighty’s saying: No, he has not yet fulfilled what he was commanded. He said: No one ever fulfills everything that was imposed upon him. Al-Baghawi narrated it on the authority of Al-Hasan Al-Basri in a similar manner, and I did not find any words from the earlier scholars on it other than this. What I find in the meaning of that, and God knows best, is that the meaning is: Then if He wills, He will resurrect him. That is, He will send him. No, he has not yet fulfilled what he was commanded. That is, he will not do it now until the period expires and the decree is fulfilled for the children of Adam, from those whom God has decreed that they will exist and come out into the world. God Almighty has commanded it in creation and in destiny. So when that reaches the end with God, God will resurrect the creation and return them as He began them. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Wahb ibn Munabbih, who said: Uzair, peace be upon him, said: The angel who came to me said: The graves are the belly of the earth, and the earth is the mother of creation. So when God creates what He wants to create and these graves that He extended are completed, the world will come to an end, and those on it will die, and the earth will vomit out what is in its belly, and the graves will bring out what is in them. This is similar to what we said about the meaning of the verse, and God Almighty knows best. And the Almighty’s saying: So let man look at his food. In it is gratitude and in it is evidence of the revival of plants from the lifeless earth to the revival of bodies after they were rotten bones and torn dust. We poured down water in torrents. That is, We sent it down from the sky to the earth. Then We split the earth open. That is, We made it settle in it, so it entered its borders and penetrated the parts of the grain deposited in it, so it grew and rose and appeared on the surface of the earth. Then We caused to grow therein grain * And grapes and herbage. Grain is everything that is mentioned of grains, and grapes are well-known, and herbage is the alfalfa that animals eat when it is wet, and it is also called qat. Ibn Abbas, Qatadah, Ad-Dahhak, and As-Suddi said that. Al-Hasan Al-Basri said: The herbage is fodder. And olives. It is well-known, and it is fat, and its juice is fat, and it is used for lighting and anointing. And palm trees. It is eaten as dates, unripe dates, fresh dates, and dried dates, raw or cooked, and from which syrup and vinegar are squeezed. And gardens in abundance. That is, orchards. Al-Hasan and Qatadah said: Ghalban is palm trees. Ghalaaz Karam, Ibn Abbas and Mujahid said: Everything that is intertwined and gathered. Ibn Abbas also said: Ghalaban, the tree that provides shade under, and Ali bin Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And tall gardens meaning tall, and Ikrimah said: Ghalaban means thick-necked. In another narration: Ghalaaz ar-Raqab, have you not seen a man who has a thick neck, it is said: By God, he is the most victorious, narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim. Ibn Jarir recited for al-Farazdaq: He howled and aroused the wrath of the oppressor, so woe to Ibn al-Maragha for what he aroused. And the Almighty said: And fruits and grass. As for fruit, it is everything that is enjoyed from fruits. Ibn Abbas said: Fruit is everything that is eaten fresh, and grass is what the earth produces that animals eat but people do not eat. In a narration from him: It is grass for animals. Mujahid, Saeed bin Jubair and Abu Malik said: The father is the grass. Mujahid, Al-Hasan, Qatadah and Ibn Zayd said: The father is to animals as fruit is to humans. Ata’ said: Everything that grows on the face of the earth is the father. Ad-Dahhak said: Everything that the earth grows except fruit is the father. Ibn Idris said, on the authority of Asim ibn Kulaib, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Ab is the plant of the earth that animals eat but people do not eat. Ibn Jarir narrated it through three chains of transmission on the authority of Ibn Idris. Then he said: Abu Kurayb and Abu al-Sa’ib told us: Ibn Idris told us, Abdul-Malik told us, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, who said: Ibn Abbas counted and said: Ab is what the earth produces for livestock. This is the wording of the hadith of Abu Kurayb. Abu al-Sa’ib said in his hadith: What the earth produces of what people eat and livestock eat. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Ab is the grass and pasture. Mujahid, al-Hasan, Qatadah, Ibn Zayd, and others said the same. Abu Ubaid al-Qasim ibn Salam said: Muhammad ibn Yazid told us, al-A’wam ibn Hawshab told us, on the authority of Ibrahim al-Taymi, who said: Abu Bakr al-Siddiq may God be pleased with him was asked about the verse: And fruits and herbage. He said: Which sky will shade me and which land will bear me if I say about the Book of God what I do not know? In it is gratitude and in it is evidence of the revival of plants from the lifeless earth to the revival of bodies after they were rotten bones and torn dust. We poured down water in torrents. That is, We sent it down from the sky to the earth. Then We split the earth open. That is, We made it settle in it, so it entered its borders and penetrated the parts of the grain deposited in it, so it grew and rose and appeared on the surface of the earth. Ibn Abbas, Qatadah, Ad-Dahhak, and As-Suddi said that. Al-Hasan Al-Basri said: The herbage is fodder. And olives. It is well-known, and it is fat, and its juice is fat, and it is used for lighting and anointing. And palm trees. It is eaten as dates, unripe dates, fresh dates, and dried dates, raw or cooked, and from which syrup and vinegar are squeezed. And gardens in abundance. That is, orchards. Al-Hasan and Qatadah said: Ghalban is palm trees. Ghalaaz Karam, Ibn Abbas and Mujahid said: Everything that is intertwined and gathered. Ibn Abbas also said: Ghalaban, the tree that provides shade under, and Ali bin Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And tall gardens meaning tall, and Ikrimah said: Ghalaban means thick-necked. In another narration: Ghalaaz ar-Raqab, have you not seen a man who has a thick neck, it is said: By God, he is the most victorious, narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim. Ibn Jarir recited for al-Farazdaq: He howled and aroused the wrath of the oppressor, so woe to Ibn al-Maragha for what he aroused. And the Almighty said: And fruits and grass. Mujahid, Al-Hasan, Qatadah and Ibn Zayd said: The father is to animals as fruit is to humans. Ata’ said: Everything that grows on the face of the earth is the father. Ad-Dahhak said: Everything that the earth grows except fruit is the father. Ibn Idris said, on the authority of Asim ibn Kulaib, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Ab is the plant of the earth that animals eat but people do not eat. Ibn Jarir narrated it through three chains of transmission on the authority of Ibn Idris. Then he said: Abu Kurayb and Abu al-Sa’ib told us: Ibn Idris told us, Abdul-Malik told us, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, who said: Ibn Abbas counted and said: Ab is what the earth produces for livestock. 80:33: Ibn Abbas said: The Noise Scream is one of the names of the Day of Resurrection, which God has made great and warned His servants about. Ibn Jarir said: Perhaps it is a name for the blowing of the trumpet. Al-Baghawi said: The Noise Scream means the shout on the Day of Resurrection. It was called this because it will deafen the ears, i.e., it will be heard so loudly that it will almost deafen them. The Day when a man will flee from his brother, his mother, his father, his wife, and his children, meaning he will see them and flee from them and stay away from them because the terror will be great and the matter will be serious. Ikrimah said: A man will meet his wife and say to her: O, what a husband was I to you? She will say: What a good husband I was, and will praise him as much as she can. He will say to her: Today I ask of you one good deed that you give me so that I may be saved from what you see. She will say: How easy that you have asked for is, but I cannot give you something that I fear as much as you fear. He said: A man will meet his son and cling to him, and he will say: O, my son, what a father was I to you? He will praise him with good. He will say to him: O my son, I need an atom's weight of your good deeds so that I may be saved from what you see. His son will say: O my father, what you have asked for is easy, but I fear the same as you fear, so I cannot give you anything.
